codeReview.summary: The commit correctly records native arm64 CI success and infeasibility probes, but the deferred arm64 post-boot command set is not fully executable as written, so expectedBehavior for complete deferred boot/health-check commands is not fully met.

issues.description: Post-boot check uses `socat` against `/tmp/arm64-oracle10-qemu-monitor.sock`, but the boot command never creates this monitor socket (no `-monitor unix:...` in the QEMU invocation), so this health-check command cannot run.

The QEMU boot command provides no guest-access channel (no host forwarding/SSH setup and no command-injection mechanism), while required post-boot checks (`systemctl --failed`, `journalctl`) are only provided as commented examples (lines 193, 216, 220). This leaves the deferred post-boot validation block incomplete/non-executable.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Feature metadata requires `validation-worker`, but the skill content is missing from shared state, forcing fallback to `mission-worker-base` during execution.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Feature entry sets `skillName: validation-worker` in mission features.json; `/home/sandbox/kairos-init/.factory/skills/validation-worker` is empty (no `SKILL.md`); transcript skeleton and handoff.skillFeedback note fallback because validation-worker was unavailable.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission procedure references `.factory/services.yaml`, but the file is absent, so service/command setup is not documented in shared state.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Read of `/home/sandbox/kairos-init/.factory/services.yaml` returns ENOENT; no `services.yaml`/`services.yml` exists under `/home/sandbox/kairos-init/.factory`.
